problem: Add hlx inspect netsuite and hlx run CLI commands as thin interfaces to the server-side inspection proxy endpoints for NetSuite SuiteQL/logs and arbitrary SuiteScript execution. Both use existing inspection token auth and hxFetch HTTP client. Environment selection via --env prod|sandbox with per-step defaults from manifest.

files.why: NEW (60 lines) — cmdNetsuite handler: two modes (query via POST type='query', logs via POST type='logs'). Reads manifest nsDefaultEnv for default --env. Flags: --env, --query, --script-id. POSTs to /{repoId}/netsuite.
NEW (53 lines) — cmdRun handler: --repo required, --env/--code/--modules optional. Reads manifest nsDefaultEnv. Parses --modules as comma-separated. POSTs to /{repoId}/run.
MOD — 'netsuite' case (lines 125-138) in inspect subcommand router switch. Imports cmdNetsuite from ./netsuite.js. Validates --repo flag, delegates to handler.
MOD — 'run' case (lines 101-105) in main command dispatcher switch. Imports cmdRun from ./run/index.js. Uses configOrHelp for auth.

BOUNDARY — hxFetch (lines 37-41): basePath /api/inspect, auth via X-API-Key (hxi_ prefix) or Bearer token, retry with exponential backoff (3 attempts, 2s base delay), 30s timeout. Used by both handlers.
BOUNDARY — resolveRepo: resolves repo name or ID to internal ID via repos endpoint. Used by both handlers.
BOUNDARY — getFlag and getPositionalArgs: CLI argument parsing. Handles --repo, --env, --query, --script-id, --code, --modules.
BOUNDARY — HxConfig type with token, baseUrl, orgId. Auth from HELIX_INSPECT_TOKEN (sandbox) or HELIX_API_KEY or config file.
REFERENCE — Template pattern: resolveRepo -> hxFetch POST /{repoId}/database -> console.log JSON. 12 lines.
REFERENCE — Logs handler with optional --limit flag pattern. 14 lines.
EXECUTION — Build: tsc. Test: tsc && node --test dist/**/*.test.js. Typecheck: tsc --noEmit. Zero runtime deps. ES2022/Node16.

facts: Both netsuite.ts and run/index.ts are fully implemented and follow existing inspect handler patterns.
Both handlers read /tmp/helix-inspect/manifest.json for nsDefaultEnv to determine default --env value. Mapping: PRODUCTION->'prod', else->'sandbox'.
netsuite.ts supports two modes: query (body type='query' with query string) and logs (body type='logs' with optional scriptId). First positional arg 'logs' triggers log mode.
run/index.ts: --repo required (validated with process.exit(1)), --env optional, --code flag or positional args for code, --modules as comma-separated string.
hxFetch uses basePath /api/inspect. All requests go to /api/inspect/{repoId}/{endpoint}. Auth auto-detected from token prefix.
Build: tsc only. No Prisma, no bundling. CI: build-release.yml + publish.yml.
Zero runtime npm dependencies. Only devDependencies: @types/node, typescript.
ES2022 target, Node16 module resolution, strict TypeScript. Output in dist/.
netsuite.ts line 12: maps manifest nsDefaultEnv 'PRODUCTION'->'prod', otherwise->'sandbox'.
No test files exist for the inspect handlers or run handler. Test framework: Node.js built-in test runner.
unknowns: Whether the CLI should handle the HTTP 400 error from unavailable credentials with a user-friendly message (currently hxFetch propagates the error as-is, which includes the server's descriptive message).
Whether test files for netsuite.ts or run/index.ts are needed — no existing inspect handler tests found as precedent.
